sources.entry: datannur - Lightweight data catalog for documenting and exploring structured data files and databases. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Python

summary.one_liner: datannur is an open-source data catalog that runs from static files in the browser, with no server or database, for documenting and exploring structured data files and databases.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains the datannur web app, which runs from a single index.html and is bundled by the datannurpy Python builder when a catalog is created. The README says the catalog can be generated as portable static files and explored in the browser, then shared from a local folder, shared drive, web server, or cloud storage. It lists supported sources including CSV, Excel, ODS, Parquet, Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, SAS, SPSS, Stata, many geospatial formats, and relational databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, SQLite, and DuckDB. The app organizes metadata around eight core concepts: Organization, Folder, Tag, Concept, Doc, Dataset, Variable, and Enumeration. The interface is available in English, French, German, and Italian, with browser language detection. A separate datannur-template repository can publish a catalog on GitHub Pages.
use_cases: Document a folder of CSV or Excel files as a browsable catalog
Catalog tables from PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, or DuckDB databases
Share a data catalog from a shared drive or web server
Publish an open-data catalog on GitHub Pages
Explore variable and dataset metadata in the browser
Build a static, portable data dictionary for a team
how_to_run: Create a catalog.yml that lists folders or databases under 'add'
notable: Runs from static files with no server or database required
Single index.html app that can be opened locally or hosted anywhere static
Catalogs many file formats and relational databases through the datannurpy builder
Browser-isolated app with no direct system access
Ready-made GitHub Pages template for publishing a public catalog
caveats: Public repositories expose all data files, so sensitive data should be built locally with datannurpy
This repository holds the app itself; cataloging real sources requires the separate datannurpy builder
